title: Postfix to Minimal Infix Expression
description:
Given a valid space-separated **postfix (Reverse Polish Notation)** expression `expr` consisting of single lowercase variables (`'a'`-`'z'`) and binary operators `'+'`, `'-'`, and `'*'`, convert it into an equivalent infix expression (without spaces) using the **minimum number of parentheses** needed to preserve the exact evaluation semantics.

Standard precedence and associativity rules apply:
- `'*'` has higher precedence than `'+'` and `'-'`.
- `'+'` and `'-'` have equal precedence and associate left-to-right.
- A left operand needs parentheses if and only if its root operator has strictly lower precedence than the parent operator; a right operand needs parentheses if its root operator has strictly lower precedence, or equal precedence when the parent operator is `'-'`.
constraints: Tokens are separated by single spaces; each token is a single lowercase letter 'a'-'z' or one of '+', '-', '*'.
hints: Maintain a stack where each entry stores (infixString, rootPrecedence), with variables having precedence 3, '*' having precedence 2, and '+'/'-' having precedence 1.
When popping right then left for operator op with precedence p, wrap left iff leftPrec < p and wrap right iff rightPrec < p or (rightPrec == p and op == '-').

examples.explanation: (a + b) has lower precedence than '*', so it becomes "(a+b)*c".
a - (b - c) requires parentheses on the right child because '-' is non-associative, yielding "a-(b-c)".
a + (b * c) needs no parentheses because '*' has higher precedence than '+', yielding "a+b*c".
